seoTitle: How to Remove Jotform Branding From Your Site
metaDescription: Turn off the Powered by Jotform footer through your account settings, what plan tier it actually requires, and the branding this one toggle can't remove.
intro: The default "Powered by Jotform" footer is a small thing, but it undercuts an otherwise polished, custom-branded site, especially if you're an agency handing a form off to a client. Turning it off isn't buried in the form builder itself; it's an account-wide setting, which means it's easy to look in the wrong place. This guide covers finding the branding toggle, the specific plan tiers that unlock it, and the branding this setting doesn't touch even after you've turned it off.
prerequisites: A Jotform account on Bronze, Silver, or Gold — branding removal isn't available on the free Starter plan
costNote: Branding removal is gated to paid plans. It's included starting at Bronze, Silver, or Gold, with no separate add-on fee once the account is on a qualifying plan.

steps.heading: Open Settings from your profile menu
steps.body: Click your avatar in the top-right corner of any Jotform screen to open the account dropdown. It shows your plan tier at a glance, a Forms usage bar, an Upgrade Your Plan button, and links to Admin Console, Settings, and Logout. Click Settings. Branding controls live here, at the account level, not inside any individual form's build view, which is the detail that sends most people looking in the wrong place first.

image.caption: The account dropdown from the profile avatar, showing plan usage and the Settings link where branding controls actually live.

steps.heading: Uncheck the Jotform Branding checkbox
steps.body: On the Settings page, scroll past general account options such as Sender Emails, Form Caches, and Bounce List until you reach the Jotform Branding section. It has a single checkbox labeled "Show 'Powered by Jotform' on my forms," next to an Upgrade Account button. Uncheck it and the footer tag comes off your forms, your Visual Reports, your apps, and your Sign Documents going forward. Right below it is a separate White Label Jotform option, a bigger, Enterprise-level feature for building your own brand into the platform itself, and it's not required just to drop the footer text.

image.caption: The Jotform Branding setting, with the "Powered by Jotform" checkbox and an Upgrade Account button next to it.

steps.heading: Know what this toggle does not remove
steps.body: This one setting is narrower than it looks. It doesn't touch autoresponder emails that were already set up before you unchecked it; those keep the old branding until you open and resave each one by hand. It also can't remove the Jotform name from your form's own URL, from the Jotform logo in email digest headers, or from the terms-of-service and policy links a respondent sees if they click through from your form. None of that is a bug. It's simply outside what the branding checkbox controls, and only the Enterprise White Label option changes it.

steps.heading: Confirm the change on the form, then refresh embeds
steps.body: The Upgrade Account button next to the checkbox is a real signal: branding removal requires moving off the free Starter plan to Bronze, Silver, or Gold. If the checkbox won't stay checked, or reverts after you save, that's your plan tier, not a bug, and upgrading is the fix. If your form is embedded on a website, WordPress or otherwise, the embed frame can keep showing the old footer even after your account setting updates. Refresh the page it's embedded on, and clear any caching plugin on a WordPress site, so visitors see the change right away instead of after their next cache expiry.

troubleshooting.cause: The account is on the free Starter plan, which doesn't support branding removal.
troubleshooting.fix: Upgrade to Bronze, Silver, or Gold; the checkbox will hold once the plan supports it.

troubleshooting.problem: A confirmation email still shows 'Powered by Jotform' after you turned branding off
troubleshooting.cause: That particular autoresponder email was created before you changed the setting, and existing autoresponders don't update retroactively.
troubleshooting.fix: Open that autoresponder in the form's own Settings and resave it.

troubleshooting.problem: The old footer still shows on an embedded WordPress page
troubleshooting.cause: The embed frame or a WordPress caching plugin is still serving a cached copy of the form.
troubleshooting.fix: Refresh the page and clear the site's cache, or the cache plugin specifically if one is active.

faq.question: Is removing Jotform branding available on the free plan?
faq.answer: No. It requires upgrading from the free Starter plan to Bronze, Silver, or Gold.

faq.question: Does this also remove branding from confirmation emails?
faq.answer: Only partly. It clears branding going forward, but autoresponder emails that already existed before you turned the setting off keep the old footer until you open and resave each one. The Jotform logo in account-level email digest headers is unaffected either way.

faq.question: Will removing branding affect an already-embedded form on WordPress?
faq.answer: You may need to refresh the embed, and clear any WordPress caching plugin, before the unbranded version shows to visitors.

faq.question: Can I remove branding from individual forms only?
faq.answer: No, the toggle is account-wide. It applies to every form on the account at once, not one at a time.

faq.question: Does this remove the Jotform name from my form's URL?
faq.answer: No. The branding checkbox only removes the visible footer tag. Jotform's name stays in the form's own URL and in the linked terms-of-service and policy pages regardless of plan, unless you move to Enterprise's White Label option instead.
